red_flags.description: Class-action litigation by Troy and Lorie Gratke alleging seal failure in eleven 400 Series Tilt-Wash windows caused mold and fungus growth within four years of installation. Filed in U.S. District Court, Minneapolis. Sought damages exceeding $50,000 per claim across eight counts including breach of contract, breach of express and implied warranty, consumer protection violations, unjust enrichment, reckless misrepresentation, and negligence. Complaint alleged Andersen's fix only slowed decay.

TINA.org filed complaint with FTC in July 2025 alleging Renewal by Andersen (Andersen subsidiary) violated FTC Made in USA Labeling Rule by advertising 'Custom Built in the USA' while disclosing in fine print that products contain imported parts. Potential penalties of $53,088 per violation. Over $400 million in advertising spend implicated since January 2023. Does not directly affect 400 Series product quality but raises corporate ethics and transparency concerns.

February 26, 2026 recall of approximately 91,000 window opening control devices for 100 Series casement windows. Devices found to break or detach after impact, posing fall and serious injury hazards. Eight malfunction reports filed; no injuries. Free in-home repair by authorized technicians offered. Does not apply to 400 Series double-hung product line reviewed here.

Multiple independent owner reports across BBB, Houzz, and specialty forums document interior vinyl film delamination (blistering and bubbling) on 400 Series windows installed in the 2000s, with failures emerging consistently at 10–15 years post-installation after the non-glass warranty expires. Andersen reportedly declined warranty assistance citing expired 10-year term. Pattern appears across multiple geographic locations and installation contexts.

Corroborating reports across BBB and homeowner forums document seal failure causing water intrusion, wood rot, and mold growth in 400 Series Tilt-Wash windows. One owner reports identical failure pattern on second Andersen purchase 20 years after experiencing the same problem on a prior installation. Litigation corroborates the pattern as systemic rather than isolated.

bottom_line: The Andersen 400 Series double-hung window is a solid mid-tier clad-wood product that delivers reliable performance when professionally installed in appropriate applications, but carries meaningful documented vulnerabilities that warrant careful pre-purchase consideration. Professional installers consistently praise its manufacturing precision and position it competitively against Marvin Integrity at lower cost. Its transferable Owner-2-Owner warranty and ENERGY STAR qualification across most climate zones represent genuine value differentiators. However, three categories of evidence undermine a straightforward recommendation: (1) air infiltration performance degrades substantially with window size, meaning large 400 Series double-hungs may not perform to the same standard as smaller units despite sharing the same product designation; (2) corroborating patterns of seal failure causing mold growth and interior vinyl delamination at 10–15 years post-installation suggest systemic vulnerabilities that emerge outside of warranty coverage periods; and (3) the warranty's exclusion of all labor costs and its broad installation-related carve-outs significantly narrow practical coverage compared to marketing descriptions. Installation quality is the single most consequential variable in performance outcomes—arguably as important as the product itself—yet the warranty structure places failure causation disputes in Andersen's favor. The 400 Series is best suited for mid-size replacement windows installed by competent professionals in non-coastal environments, where its value proposition is strongest. It should be approached cautiously for oversized applications, coastal salt-air environments, or any scenario involving DIY installation without professional water management expertise.
